"Billion" is in the second half of its run, with about a third of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Billion's prize setup is not better or worse than any other. Some games pay many small prizes and some pay a few large ones.

If you play "Billion" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
762.headline: Where this game is in its run

827.body:
"50th Anniversary" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game built around small prizes that are won often. Of its unclaimed prize money, about two-thirds is in wins under $5,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

The numbers for "50th Anniversary" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
827.headline: Where the prize money is

847.body:
The $500,000 top prize on "Bingo 50X" is no longer available because all four have been claimed. The biggest prize anyone can win today is $100,000. Use that amount when you decide.

If "Bingo 50X" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
